name: Salt River (Lower Salt, Tonto NF)
gaugeName: Salt River below Stewart Mountain Dam, AZ
blurb: Dam-release tubing and kayaking reach below Saguaro Lake in the Tonto National Forest. Flow depends on releases from Stewart Mountain Dam. Tonto Pass required at the sites.

sections.putIn: Water Users Day Use Area (Lower Salt)
sections.takeOut: Blue Point Day Use Area (Lower Salt)
sections.notes: Miles (2.4) are NHD High Resolution centreline-routed between the agency points; no agency mileage found. Tonto NF: 'Caution: Fallen trees and other materials in the river can trap swimmers and floaters'. Glass containers prohibited; day use only (Lower Salt special occupancy order 03-12-03-23-39). The reach sits below Stewart Mountain Dam, so check USGS 09502000 before going.
sections.mapPendingReason: Blue Point Day Use Area (Lower Salt): Research-only grade: access-verified (official source names boating access; approximate area only). Imagery: the point is in the day-use parking lot about 110 m east of the river channel. v1.3: North's owner-supplied point (33.5539720, -111.5750868) is at the water's edge on the beach just south of the Bush Highway bridge (NHD 49 m, river right), but that beach is on the Pebble Beach side of the highway (175 m from the Pebble Beach page coordinate, 193 m from the Blue Point one), so it was not applied. v1.4: reassessed with North's statement that Sheeps Crossing is the other side (his Sheeps point is river-left, 432 m away) and the USFS INFRA site points (Pebble Beach 95705 serves the south lots; Blue Point 95316 is the lot north of the highway); still not applied (research/replacement-proposals-AZ.json). Official source names boating access, but the exact water-entry point is not pinned by an agency coordinate confirmed on imagery.

sections.putIn: Water Users Day Use Area (Lower Salt)
sections.takeOut: Phon D Sutton Day Use Area (Lower Salt)
sections.notes: Miles (8.8) are NHD High Resolution centreline-routed between the agency points; no agency mileage found. Full Tonto day-use reach; fallen trees, eagle closure zone near Goldfield Dec 1-Jun 30. Phon D Sutton is the last take-out in this package: the next site, Granite Reef (above Granite Reef Diversion Dam), is closure-uncertain.

putInAccess.operator: USDA Forest Service (Tonto NF, Mesa Ranger District)
putInAccess.sourceName: Access: USDA Forest Service, Tonto NF: Water Users Day Use Area (Site Open). Coordinate: North's own Google Maps marking (owner-supplied), checked on Esri World Imagery
putInAccess.note: IMAGERY-PLACED: coordinate is owner-supplied (North's own Google Maps satellite marking, 33.5541561, -111.5433992) and checked on Esri World Imagery z19 on 2026-10-26 (research/raw/imagery/water_users_day_use_area_lower_salt_owner_z19.png); it is NOT an agency coordinate. On imagery: North's point sits on the open sand clearing where the foot paths from the day-use parking lot reach the north bank, about 10-20 m from the channel edge across a bare silt/gravel bar; no constructed ramp (natural shore launch). The USFS EDW point (recareaid 35407) is in the paved lot about 156 m north. The waterline moves with Stewart Mountain Dam releases. NHD High Resolution flowline 37 m away. Superseded agency point: USFS EDW Recreation Opportunities, recareaid 35407 'Water Users Day Use Area' (same coordinate on the Tonto NF page) at 33.555518, -111.543833 (https://apps.fs.usda.gov/arcx/rest/services/EDW/EDW_RecreationOpportunities_01/MapServer/0/query?where=recareaid%3D35407&outFields=*&outSR=4326&f=json). Legal boating access: USDA Forest Service, Tonto NF: Water Users Day Use Area (Site Open) (https://www.fs.usda.gov/r03/tonto/recreation/water-users-day-use-area): 'Water Users is a popular site for kayakers and tubers.' 'This site is most popular as a launch site' 'Motorized boats are not allowed to launch at this site.' Tonto Daily Pass (and Watercraft Sticker, if required). Spot-check this point first; imagery date is not published by Esri.
putInAccess.bankSourceName: USGS NHD High Resolution flowline (flow-direction digitized) + Esri World Imagery
putInAccess.bankNote: Facing downstream (flow bearing ~247), the point is right of the NHD centreline (37 m).

takeOutAccess.operator: USDA Forest Service (Tonto NF, Mesa Ranger District)
takeOutAccess.sourceName: Access: USDA Forest Service, Tonto NF: Phon D Sutton Day Use Area (Site Open). Coordinate: North's own Google Maps marking (owner-supplied), checked on Esri World Imagery
takeOutAccess.note: IMAGERY-PLACED: coordinate is owner-supplied (North's own Google Maps satellite marking, 33.5465461, -111.6616464) and checked on Esri World Imagery z19 on 2026-10-26 (research/raw/imagery/phon_d_sutton_day_use_area_lower_salt_owner_z19.png); it is NOT an agency coordinate. On imagery: North's point sits at the waterline on the south bank of the Salt, on an open sandy/rocky shore reached by foot paths from the western Phon D Sutton parking lots and ramadas, just below the Verde River confluence (the Verde enters from the north opposite). No constructed ramp (natural shore take-out). The Tonto NF page point (EDW recareaid 35397) is in the eastern parking lot about 420 m east (60 m south of the river there); the paved site road links both lot groups, and EDW lists no other recreation site between Raccoon Bluff (1.7 km upstream) and this point. The waterline moves with Salt and Verde dam releases. NHD High Resolution flowline 17 m away. Superseded agency point: Tonto NF Phon D Sutton page coordinate (USFS EDW Recreation Opportunities recareaid 35397 'Phon D Sutton Day Use Area': 33.547016, -111.657843) at 33.54697106, -111.6571505 (https://apps.fs.usda.gov/arcx/rest/services/EDW/EDW_RecreationOpportunities_01/MapServer/0/query?where=recareaid%3D35397&outFields=*&outSR=4326&f=json). Legal boating access: USDA Forest Service, Tonto NF: Phon D Sutton Day Use Area (Site Open) (https://www.fs.usda.gov/r03/tonto/recreation/phon-d-sutton-day-use-area): 'This site is a popular inner tube take-out point.' Tonto Daily Pass (and Watercraft Sticker, if required). Spot-check this point first; imagery date is not published by Esri.
takeOutAccess.bankSourceName: USGS NHD High Resolution flowline (flow-direction digitized) + Esri World Imagery
takeOutAccess.bankNote: Facing downstream (flow bearing ~250), the point is left of the NHD centreline (17 m). Imagery agrees: the point, the parking lots and the site road are on the south bank (river left when facing downstream, flow to the west-southwest).
